sections.html:
Nebraska has no estate tax. What it has is an inheritance tax, which the person who receives property pays, not the estate. County court determines it, and the county treasurer takes the payment and the required report.

Federal estate tax is a separate matter. It only applies to estates above $15,000,000 for people who die in 2026, so most Nebraska families never meet it. The state inheritance tax is the one that reaches ordinary households, and it can reach a house.

What an heir owes depends on how closely related the heir was to the person who died. Nebraska sorts heirs into three classes under statutes 77-2004, 77-2005 and 77-2006.

For deaths on or after January 1, 2023, close relatives pay 1%, aunts, uncles, nieces and nephews pay 11%, and everyone else pays 15%. Each heir first gets an exempt amount.

ClassWho is includedRateTaxed on amount over
Class 1Parents, grandparents, siblings, children, lineal descendants, and their spouses1%$100,000
Class 2Aunts, uncles, nieces, nephews and their lineal descendants, and their spouses11%$40,000
Class 3All other persons, including friends and non-relatives15%$25,000

The tax is measured on the clear market value of what each person receives. Court decisions annotated under the statute treat that as fair market value on the date of death, minus anything the heir paid for the property.

Class 1 also takes in a person the decedent treated as a child for at least ten years before death, along with that person's descendants. Nebraska courts have weighed factors like support, discipline, shared time and written evidence when deciding whether that relationship existed.

A surviving spouse owes nothing on what passes to them, and neither does an heir under 22 years old in any class. Under 77-2004, interests passing to a surviving spouse by will or any other route are outside the tax.

  • Anyone whose inheritance stays at or below the exempt amount for their class.
  • A person under 22 receiving an interest, whichever of the three classes applies.
  • The homestead allowance, exempt property and family maintenance allowance.
  • Bequests in trust to an in-state association for exclusively charitable purposes in Nebraska.

These exemptions decide whether selling an inherited house leaves a tax bill behind. A house going to a spouse is outside the tax. The same house going to adult children is taxed only on the value above $100,000 for each child.

sections.h2: How the exempt amount and rate work together
sections.html:
Think of each heir's share as its own calculation. Take what that person receives, subtract the exempt amount for their class, and apply the class rate to the remainder. A Class 1 heir pays 1% on value beyond $100,000, a Class 2 heir pays 11% on value beyond $40,000, and a Class 3 heir pays 15% on value beyond $25,000.

When a house is split among several heirs, each share is measured on its own against that person's exempt amount. A share that lands at or below the exempt amount produces no tax, even if the whole house is worth much more than that. This is why a house left to two or three children can come out tax-free while the same house left to one friend does not.

Deductions are listed in 77-2018.04, and the county judge determines and assesses the final amount. Use the class rates as a rough guide to the size of the issue and ask the county court for the real figure.

The tax is due 12 months after the date of death. Interest runs on unpaid tax from that date at the rate in section 45-104.01.

If no proceeding to determine the tax is filed in those 12 months, a penalty of 5% per month or part of a month is added, up to 25% of the unpaid tax. Filing a probate petition or application counts as an appropriate proceeding. So does filing for a tentative payment and paying it inside the 12 months. The county court can abate the penalty for good cause.

A tentative payment helps when the house is listed or under contract but the final figure is not set. Under 77-2018.07 you apply in writing to the county court. If the county attorney does not consent, the county attorney has seven days to state a different amount, and the payment can be amended later. It covers probate and nonprobate estates, and it stops interest and penalty from building while the numbers are settled.

sections.h2: How the tax is determined and who files what
sections.html:
The county court can determine the inheritance tax inside a probate case or in a proceeding opened only for that purpose. The court itself can start it, and so can the personal representative, the county attorney, or anyone with a legal interest in the property (77-2018.01).

After tax is paid, the person who filed the proceeding sends the county treasurer a Form PCIT, the Petitioner's County Inheritance Tax Report. It is due when the court order determining the tax is entered. The form counts beneficiaries and tax paid by class and by residency, and no inheritance tax can be paid or refunded before a required report is in.

"Petitioner" is defined broadly. It can be a personal representative, a trustee, someone who filed an affidavit to transfer real property without probate, or the beneficiary of a transfer on death deed. A house passing outside probate can therefore still call for paperwork at the county.

sections.h2: Selling before the tax is paid
sections.html:
A house can be sold while the inheritance tax is still open. Selling does not erase the tax, which is figured on the value each heir received, so plan early and have the money ready.

Your route to clear title depends on how the estate is handled:

  • With a personal representative, the representative signs a deed of distribution to the heirs, who then sell. That deed is on the state's documentary stamp tax exemption list, though the later sale to a buyer is not.
  • Without probate, an heir can use the affidavit for transfer of real property if at least 30 days have gone by since death, no personal representative has been appointed or applied for, and the Nebraska real property is worth $100,000 or less on the assessment rolls after real estate taxes owed. The other heirs must sign too.
  • With a transfer on death deed, the deed is recorded and a death certificate is filed. The state exempts these deeds from the stamp tax.

Creditors can reach an affidavit successor only up to the value of what was inherited, and that claim ends three years after death or one year after distribution, whichever is later. Our Nebraska probate guide covers the court route in more detail.

Each deed recorded in Nebraska needs a Real Estate Transfer Statement, Form 521, under 76-214, and the register of deeds will not record without it. When the deed follows a death, the statement can ask for the date of death and whether title changed through a transfer on death deed, joint tenancy or the end of a life estate.

The documentary stamp tax on a non-exempt sale is $3.32 per $1,000 of value for deeds recorded on or after July 18, 2026. Before that it was $2.32. The estate or heirs selling the house pay it as grantor, in addition to any inheritance tax owed by individual heirs.

Heirs who would rather not carry the house through listing and repairs can ask Cash Home Buyers for an as-is cash offer. A cash sale closes without a buyer's loan approval, and the title company pays the recording charges and any taxes owed from the proceeds. This page is general information, not legal or tax advice, so confirm your own numbers with the county court or an attorney.

faqs.q: Does Nebraska have an estate tax?
faqs.a: No. Nebraska charges an inheritance tax instead, paid by the person who receives the property. Federal estate tax applies only above $15,000,000 for 2026 deaths.

faqs.q: How much inheritance tax would my child owe on a Nebraska house?
faqs.a: A child is a Class 1 heir, so the rate is 1% on the value received above $100,000. A child whose share stays at or below $100,000 owes nothing.

faqs.q: Does a surviving spouse pay Nebraska inheritance tax?
faqs.a: No. Interests passing to a surviving spouse by will or any other means are not subject to the tax under Neb. Rev. Stat. 77-2004.

faqs.q: When is Nebraska inheritance tax due?
faqs.a: 12 months after the date of death. Interest runs on unpaid tax from that date, and a penalty of 5% per month, up to 25%, can apply if no proceeding is filed in time.

faqs.q: Can I pay part of the tax before the final amount is set?
faqs.a: Yes. A tentative payment can be made after a written application to the county court, with the county attorney's consent or a court order, and it can be adjusted later.
